analysis: Both units are unchanged base-side context (base lines 1629-2248) of docs/architecture/inference.md. The only change in this file is a documentation addition at head lines 1370-1382. It describes Qwen inline MTP ordinary-decode history chaining and the prefill carry, the per-drafter opt-in supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory, and the rollback env switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. That change is outside these units and is only visible via the patch excerpt. The surrounding context covers MiMo native ownership, media decode accounting, prefix-cache bindings, Flint protocol constraints and Bonsai MTP. I reviewed it against T-041 (prefix cache and cacheSalt scoping), TB-007 and T-028 (in-process inference memory), and T-010 and T-029 (DoS and leases). The documented change is a performance and speculative-decode behavior. It does not alter the SSD prefix-cache gate, TTL, HMAC naming, cacheSalt plumbing, encryption or attestation paths. MTP remains fail-open to target-only decode (base invariant 7, line 1977). The new switches are rollback controls, not security gates. Integration should confirm one point in the implementation (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory), which is not supplied here. Assistant history and carry must be strictly per-request row and must not mix hidden states across concurrent tenants' decode rows. Cross-row contamination would be an A-001 / TB-007 confidentiality and correctness concern. The docs say rows are appended in step order to the assistant history for the single speculating row; that wording should be verified as per-row. No regression was identified from the documentation alone.
